title: Story Sums to 10
seo_title: Grade R Story Sums Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade R: Problem solving in context
standard_text: Solve word problems (story sums) in context and explain own solution to problems involving addition and subtraction with answers up to 10.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade R maths worksheets: story sums that add, take away and compare, with answers up to 10. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Listen to the story and picture it.
  • Altogether, in all, more come: add.
  • Left, ate, gave away, flew away: take away.
  • Act it out with counters, then answer the question.

Examples

Example

Lerato has 6 sweets and eats 2. How many are left?

6, take away 2

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Add or take awayLeft means take away.
The questionListen to what is asked.
One partCount both parts.

faq.a: The Reception Year, the year before Grade 1 and the first year of the Foundation Phase. Learners are about 5 to 6 years old.

faq.q: Can Grade R learners read the stories?
faq.a: An adult reads the story aloud; the learner acts it out and answers.

items.e: The parts are 4 and 3. The whole is 7.

items.q: Ayanda has 2 red pencils and 6 green pencils. How many pencils does she have?
items.e: The parts are 2 and 6. The whole is 8.

items.q: Lerato puts 3 shells in one bucket and 4 shells in another. How many shells are there?
items.e: The parts are 3 and 4. The whole is 7.

items.q: There are 6 ducks. 2 are in the pond. How many are out of the pond?
items.e: The whole is 6. One part is 2. 2 and 4 make 6.

items.q: Chloe has 6 big blocks and 2 small blocks. How many blocks is that?
items.e: The parts are 6 and 2. The whole is 8.

items.e: The parts are 4 and 4. The whole is 8.

items.e: The whole is 5. One part is 1. 1 and 4 make 5.

items.q: Ethan has 3 apples. He picks 2 more. How many apples does he have now?
items.e: 3 and 2 more make 5. 3 + 2 = 5. The answer is 5 apples.

items.q: Lerato has 1 ball. A friend gives Lerato 4 more balls. How many balls does Lerato have now?
items.e: 1 and 4 more make 5. 1 + 4 = 5. The answer is 5 balls.

items.q: Pieter sees 3 fish. Then he sees 3 more fish. How many fish does he see in all?
items.e: 3 and 3 more make 6. 3 + 3 = 6. The answer is 6 fish.
5 and 1 more make 6. 5 + 1 = 6. The answer is 6 stars.

items.q: Ethan picks 2 flowers. Then he picks 5 more. How many flowers does he pick in all?
items.e: 2 and 5 more make 7. 2 + 5 = 7. The answer is 7 flowers.

items.q: There are 4 cups on the table. Ofentse puts out 3 more. How many cups are there now?
items.e: 4 and 3 more make 7. 4 + 3 = 7. The answer is 7 cups.
6 and 2 more make 8. 6 + 2 = 8. The answer is 8 hearts.

items.q: Precious has 3 apples. She eats 1. How many apples are left?
items.e: 3 take away 1 is 2. 3 − 1 = 2. The answer is 2 apples.

items.q: 4 ducks are in a pond. 2 swim away. How many ducks are still in the pond?
items.e: 4 take away 2 is 2. 4 − 2 = 2. The answer is 2 ducks.

items.q: Tshepo has 5 balls. He gives 1 to a friend. How many balls does he have now?
items.e: 5 take away 1 is 4. 5 − 1 = 4. The answer is 4 balls.

items.q: There are 6 cups. Sibusiso breaks 2. How many cups are not broken?
items.e: 6 take away 2 is 4. 6 − 2 = 4. The answer is 4 cups.
6 take away 4 is 2. 6 − 4 = 2. The answer is 2 stickers.

items.q: 7 fish are in a tank. Pieter moves 3 to a new tank. How many fish are in the first tank now?
items.e: 7 take away 3 is 4. 7 − 3 = 4. The answer is 4 fish.

items.q: Lerato picks 7 flowers. She gives 1 to her mother. How many flowers does she have now?
items.e: 7 take away 1 is 6. 7 − 1 = 6. The answer is 6 flowers.
